name: CA-51
label: Safe D

key_factors: Incumbent Sara Jacobs running with a large fundraising edge
Prediction markets price Democratic win at ~95%
model.rationale: The fundamentals point strongly to Jacobs: a D+10 district, incumbency, and a $1.6 million warhead against a little-known, unfunded Republican challenger, with markets pricing her near-certain to win. With no polls or expert ratings to contradict that picture, the race stays firmly in Safe D territory.
model.watch: Any late polling showing a much tighter race or a surge of outside spending for Cabrera would be the first sign this is closer than expected.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Sara Jacobs, the Democratic incumbent, advanced to the general election in a San Diego-area district that leans about ten points Democratic. She has raised roughly $1.6 million and holds a clear financial advantage over Republican Ricardo Cabrera, who reports no significant fundraising. Prediction markets give Jacobs about a 95 percent chance of winning.

No public general-election polls or expert ratings are available for this race, so the forecast rests on the district's partisan lean, incumbency, and the money gap. All of these point the same direction, making Jacobs a heavy favorite to return to Congress.
